title: Counit normalization of the canonical derived comparison
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring, f : U → V a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme morphism, and K an object of D⁺(U_et, Mod_Λ). Write C_T = ι ⋙ D(ν_T^*) for the comparison on bounded-below inputs, a_f : l_f ⋙ C_U ≅ C_V ⋙ p_f for the specified left-derived pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and b_f : r_f ⋙ C_V ≅ C_U ⋙ s_f for the specified derived direct-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Here l_f ⊣ r_f is the bounded-below etale adjunction and p_f ⊣ s_f is the unbounded pro-etale adjunction. The following equality holds: a_f(r_f K) ≫ p_f(b_f(K)) ≫ ε_pro(C_U K) = C_U(ε_et(K)). The comparisons are exactly the constructions named in the attached Lean statement, including the Plus-to-unbounded comparison isomorphisms.

proof.text: Use iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_symm to identify the adjoint conjugate of lowerStarCompComparisonLowerStarIso with comparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso. The mateEquiv_counit_symm identity gives the underived counit equation. Injectivity of the adjunction hom-equivalence identifies lowerStarComparisonUpperStarBaseChange with the mate of the pullback comparison. These calculations are the private helpers underived_comparison_counit and underived_comparison_mate.

For a square of exact horizontal functors and adjunctions, form the induced comparison on D+ using mapDerivedCategoryPlusCompIso and mapDerivedCategoryPlusNatIso. Their factorization equations on the homotopy category verify the hypothesis of derivedPlus_mateEquiv_app_fac. Compare this equation with rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange_fac; uniqueness via rightDerived_ext proves that derivation of the underived mate is the mate of the derived comparison. Apply mateEquiv_counit to obtain comparison_counit_plus. All these private helpers are proved, with no new obligation.

Transport the inverse comparison through the fully faithful inclusion of D+ using the hom compatibility equations for mapDerivedCategoryPlusCompIso and mapDerivedCategoryPlusNatIso, and apply congrArg Iso.inv for the inverse equations. This proves the private comparison_iso_restrict helper.

Expand the fixed comparisons [def-weil-pbc-fixed-derived-comparisons]. Map comparison_counit_plus through the D+-inclusion. Rewrite derivedPlus as the restricted unbounded derived adjunction using derivedAdjunctionPlus_eq_derivedPlus and map_restrictFullyFaithful_counit_app. Apply comparison_iso_restrict and naturality of leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory.inv. The resulting equation is precisely the stated fixed-map identity.

theorem comparison_counit {U V : Scheme.{u}} (f : U ⟶ V)
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))) :
    (leftDerivedUpperStarComparisonIso f Λ).hom.app
        (R+(Etale.lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f).obj K) ≫
      L(ProEtale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f).map
        ((rightDerivedLowerStarComparisonIso' f (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).hom.app K) ≫
      (derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f).counit.app
        ((DerivedCategory.Plus.ι ⋙ D(ν^*(U)[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ])).obj K) =
    (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι ⋙ D(ν^*(U)[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ])).map
      ((Etale.derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunctionPlus (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f).counit.app K)
